---
title: "Readiness"
subtitle: "What works now and what remains"
---

MLPerf EDU separates local usability, quality acceptance, stability, and
production publication. The first milestone requires every authoritative path
to run on a supported local machine. One complete run is enough to evaluate a
quality target. Repeated timing runs remain later work. Thirteen paths
currently meet the local-execution requirement. MiniGo is the one remaining
blocker.

## Current Portfolio

All fourteen workloads have a public CLI path, exact target contract, asset
policy, report export, and provenance boundary. Their current quality states
are grouped below.

| **State** | **Workloads** | **Meaning** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Target met | image classification, keyword spotting, anomaly detection, visual wake words, causal language modeling, text classification, information retrieval, graph node classification | At least one complete authoritative `max` result meets the declared target. |
| Target gap recorded | time-series forecasting, code generation, function calling, image generation, recommendation, reinforcement learning | A complete provenance-bound measurement does not meet the unchanged published reproduction point. |

The [quality target review](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/QUALITY_TARGET_REVIEW.md)
records the authority and rationale behind every threshold. The
[initial usability checklist](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/STATUS.md)
contains the workload-by-workload results and remaining tasks.
The [independent audit](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md)
records the simulated student, instructor, and benchmark-review verdicts. The
[product readiness plan](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/STATUS.md)
defines the dashboard, assignment, research, and production spirals.
The [local execution plan](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/main/mlperf-edu/docs/internal/STATUS.md)
defines the remaining MiniGo, asset, resume, and acceptance work.

## Assets and Release Policy

Every workload names its exact dataset, split, model source, checkpoint or
training recipe, and evaluator. Some assets are approved for fetch-only use,
while others still require redistribution review. Local execution may require
manual terms acceptance,
but the CLI must verify the supplied bytes and run the complete quality
contract without remote compute. The CLI fails closed instead of substituting
synthetic data for an authoritative quality run.

## Normal Student Path

```bash
uv run mlperf init --profile min --output-dir submissions/first-run
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload image-classification --profile max \
  --output-dir submissions/image-classification
```

The final command writes JSON, CSV, HTML, and `.provd.json` files. The HTML
dashboard stays closed unless `--open-report` is explicit. A `min` report leads
with functional readiness,
while a quality-bearing report leads with the metric, target decision, and
normalized target attainment. Both continue with the exact configuration,
hardware, model lineage, and provenance.

The `min` result only confirms setup. A student should use `max` for a graded
quality result and preserve the complete artifact set. Every `min` and `max` path targets local hardware, MiniGo included, though its
laptop self-play budget is far below the reference contract and it therefore
records a miss rather than a quality claim.

The [numbered examples](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/examples)
turn this path into five labs with explicit controls, report-reading questions,
and instructor rubrics.

## Research Path

The `pro` profile defaults to the nine-workload research collection. An
individual workload can always be selected, and `--collection all` expands the
selection to all fourteen. Pro runs execute the max contract once by default
and preserve subrun configuration and artifacts in their aggregate result.

```bash
uv run mlperf run --profile pro --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --profile pro --collection all --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile pro
```

A versioned plan adds an explicit research question, hypothesis, independent
variables, controls, conditions, device policy, and output policy. The HTML
report shows the study design beside direction-aware quality small multiples,
and JSON and CSV retain the condition metadata for later analysis.

```bash
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml --dry-run
uv run mlperf run --plan examples/research/pro-collection/plan.yaml
```

The [pro plan example](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/examples/research/pro-collection)
uses two image-classification batch sizes while pinning the quality contract.
Optional repetition is available for later stability studies. It is not part
of the current quality-acceptance requirement.

The expected systems behavior is documented for every workload. Measured
working-set, arithmetic-intensity, and dispatch classifications remain later
research-characterization work and are reported as `unmeasured` until trace
evidence exists.

## Production Boundary

The source checkout is suitable for supervised classroom trials and bounded
research evaluation. All fourteen workloads now execute locally, but this is not a production
package or an accepted public benchmark.
Component licensing, package publication, dataset release review, MLCommons
governance, security review, independent hardware reproduction, and
authenticated release artifacts remain open production gates.
